transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. 

However, you'll want to avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them after surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be able to use your eye gel as you normally would. If you're unsure about anything specific, it's best to check with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't know exactly how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you for answering my questions, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.
